pr_title: Cache legacy keys instead of downgrading them
pr_body:
If someone calls an `EVP_PKEY_get0*()` function then we create a legacy key and cache it in the EVP_PKEY - but it doesn't become an "origin" and it doesn't ever get updated. This will be documented as a restriction of the `EVP_PKEY_get0*() `function with provided keys.

This avoids lots of multi-threading issues with the current "downgrade" approach.

Fixes #14020

While implementing this I noticed various functions that should have been deprecated that weren't. Since I was touching the man pages for these anyway, I also deprecated those while I was at it.

Fixes #14303
Fixes #14317
pr_comments: Since this is technically a breaking change I'm putting an OTC hold on this so that OTC get the chance to approve this approach. It is otherwise ready for review and I invite review comments.
I think the following manpages also need updates: man7/EVP_PKEY.pod, man3/evp_pkey_export_to_provider.pod

issue_context.title: EVP_PKEY_get0_DSA() and EVP_PKEY_get1_DSA() should be deprecated
issue_context.body: All the similar `EVP_PKEY_get(0|1)_*` functions have been deprecated. But for some reason these ones were missed.

review_comments: This seems curious...  why isn't the ameth set when creating the legacy cache pkey?
Because we really don't have a "proper" legacy key and we don't want to accidentally end up in the legacy code. We don't need it for anything other than "freeing" so we do it just-in-time.
This is an internal header file only, so that isn't appropriate here.
This interesting workaround is actually a good reason why the get1 should not be a dup() as we discussed.
